extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of New York / readers of The Independent Journal debating ratification of the U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the constitutional design and delegated powers of the U.S. Senate (e.g., treaty-making, appointments, impeachment trials) and the institutional checks intended to prevent aristocracy or corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by bodies elected by the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Two bodies ... annually ELECTED BY THE WHOLE BODY OF THE PEOPLE ... considered as the REPRESENTATIVES of the people, almost in their PLENIPOTENTIARY capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes ancient representative institutions (e.g., Ephori, Tribunes) from American governments; emphasizes legitimacy and plenipotentiary character when representatives are elected by the whole body of the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantage of representative government combined with extensive territory
rubrics_metrics.description: The true distinction ... lies IN THE TOTAL EXCLUSION OF THE PEOPLE, IN THEIR COLLECTIVE CAPACITY, from any share in the LATTER ... must be admitted to leave a most advantageous superiority in favor of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that representative government succeeds better over a large territory and that American design’s exclusion of direct collective action is deliberate and beneficial when paired with large territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect election and six-year terms do not inevitably produce tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: A senate appointed not immediately by the people, and for the term of six years, must gradually acquire a dangerous pre-eminence ... To this general answer, the general reply ought to be sufficient, that liberty may be endangered by the abuses of liberty as well as by the abuses of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that for the Senate to become tyrannical it would have to corrupt itself, state legislatures, the House, and the people — a sequence unlikely in practice; cites Maryland and ancient/British examples as empirical rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senators should be chosen by enlightened/select bodies rather than by mass popular vote
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention ... have directed the President to be chosen by select bodies of electors ... and they have committed the appointment of senators to the State legislatures. This mode has, in such cases, vastly the advantage of elections by the people in their collective capacity ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select electors and state legislatures are expected to be 'the most enlightened and respectable citizens' whose information leads to appointments of men distinguished by abilities and virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and qualification requirements to ensure known character
rubrics_metrics.description: By excluding men under thirty-five from the first office, and those under thirty from the second, it confines the electors to men of whom the people have had time to form a judgment ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age minima (President 35, senators 30) aim to ensure electors can judge candidates’ characters and are less likely to be misled by transient brilliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty power should be exercised with both deliberation and capacity for secrecy/despatch
rubrics_metrics.description: It seldom happens in the negotiation of treaties ... but that perfect SECRECY and immediate DESPATCH are sometimes requisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaty negotiation requires both the talents, information, and integrity of able men (Senate/advice & consent) and the President’s capacity for secrecy and rapid action (intelligence management). The constitutional arrangement balances these needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration in office fosters accumulation of political information and stability
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration prescribed is such as will give them an opportunity of greatly extending their political information, and of rendering their accumulating experience more and more beneficial to their country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer terms (e.g., Senate) and staggered elections preserve continuity, uniformity, and a residue of experienced officials so affairs requiring time and exact information are handled properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaties should be binding (supreme) and not unilaterally repealable by legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: They insist ... that treaties like acts of assembly, should be repealable at pleasure. This idea seems to be new and peculiar to this country ... a treaty is only another name for a bargain ... as the consent of both was essential to their formation at first, so must it ever afterwards be to alter or cancel them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues treaties are mutual bargains and thus their binding effect and supremacy are proper; unilateral repeal by one party would make foreign bargains impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate participation ensures correspondence between treaties and laws (commerce/ navigation policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of much consequence that this correspondence and conformity be carefully maintained; and they who assent ... will see and confess that it is well provided for by making concurrence of the Senate necessary both to treaties and to laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring Senate concurrence promotes coherence between negotiated treaties and domestic legislation affecting trade and navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate as an appropriate tribunal for impeachment trials (national inquest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it not designed as a method of NATIONAL INQUEST into the conduct of public men? If this be the design of it, who can so properly be the inquisitors for the nation as the representatives of the nation themselves?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate combines dignity, independence, and representative legitimacy needed to decide politically charged misconduct of public officials; House should originate impeachments and Senate try them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of a numerous, impartial tribunal for impeachments rather than a small judicial body
rubrics_metrics.description: The awful discretion which a court of impeachments must necessarily have ... forbids the commitment of the trust to a small number of persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment trials require many decision-makers to mitigate partisan passions and to avoid the perils of concentrated judicial discretion; Supreme Court would be too small or insufficiently authoritative to reconcile public acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid having same judges try impeachment and subsequent criminal prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Would it be proper that the persons who had disposed of his fame ... in one trial, should, in another trial, for the same offense, be also the disposers of his life and his fortune?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation avoids prejudicing later criminal proceedings; combining roles risks compounded error and bias against the accused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief Justice presides over Senate impeachment trial as prudent mean
rubrics_metrics.description: The benefits of that union will be obtained from making the chief justice of the Supreme Court the president of the court of impeachments ... This was perhaps the prudent mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involving the chief justice provides legal leadership without merging the judiciary into the impeachment tribunal entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial intermixture of powers is compatible with separation of powers for special purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The true meaning of this maxim ... has been shown to be entirely compatible with a partial intermixture of those departments for special purposes, preserving them, in the main, distinct and unconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining legislative and judicial functions in the Senate for impeachments is acceptable when narrowly circumscribed and serves mutual checks among branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-thirds requirement for treaty approval and conviction provides security
rubrics_metrics.description: The second section gives power to the President, 'BY AND WITH THE ADVICE AND CONSENT OF THE SENATE, TO MAKE TREATIES, PROVIDED TWO THIRDS OF THE SENATORS PRESENT CONCUR.' ... As the concurrence of two thirds of the Senate will be requisite to a condemnation, the security to innocence ... will be as complete as itself can desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supermajority thresholds (two-thirds) act as protective guardrails both for treaty-making and for conviction in impeachments, increasing stability and protecting minority or individual rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal state representation in the Senate preserves balance of state interests
rubrics_metrics.description: As all the States are equally represented in the Senate, and by men the most able and the most willing to promote the interests of their constituents, they will all have an equal degree of influence in that body ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal representation gives each state influence in treaty/appointment decisions and incentivizes states to appoint proper persons and insist on attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular branch (House) as counterpoise to Senate powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusive privilege of originating money bills will belong to the House of Representatives. The same house will possess the sole right of instituting impeachments ... The same house will be the umpire in all elections of the President ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates concrete powers of the House (money bills, impeachments, contingent presidential elections) designed to counterbalance Senate authority and prevent aristocratic ascendancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence in institutional design: accept imperfection if overall plan is good
rubrics_metrics.description: If mankind were to resolve to agree in no institution of government, until every part of it had been adjusted to the most exact standard of perfection, society would soon become a general scene of anarchy ... To answer the purpose of the adversaries ... they ought to prove ... that the plan upon the whole is bad and pernicious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for critique: those opposing the Constitution must show the whole plan is pernicious, not merely that particular provisions are imperfect; emphasizes practical prudence in institutional design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy, despatch, and intelligence-management justify executive role in treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Those matters which in negotiations usually require the most secrecy and the most despatch, are those preparatory and auxiliary measures ... For these, the President will find no difficulty to provide; and should any circumstance occur which requires the advice and consent of the Senate, he may at any time convene them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President is better suited to urgent, secret intelligence tasks; the Senate is available for deliberation when needed—combination balances competing operational demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corruptly obtained treaties are void by the law of nations
rubrics_metrics.description: But in such a case, if it should ever happen, the treaty so obtained from us would, like all other fraudulent contracts, be null and void by the law of nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a corrupt treaty were made, international law would render it void; domestic mechanisms (impeachment, reputation) and international law serve as remedies/deterrents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on personal motives and public sanctions for official fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Every consideration that can influence the human mind, such as honor, oaths, reputations, conscience, the love of country, and family affections and attachments, afford security for their fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-legal moral and reputational incentives (honor, oaths, impeachment risk) are presented as practicable guarantees of good behavior by officeholders.
